title: Run W-6: Ti-doped FeGaSe
subtitle: Strict budget: 12 measurements, 14 days · delivered B010 · failed
task: Dope FeGaSe with Ti. Above a critical Ti content the crystal structure distorts to a lower-symmetry form, and the device needs that distorted phase. Deliver a sample that is only the distorted phase, whose magnetic ordering temperature (where its magnetic order sets in) is 123.6 ± 3.0 K and whose oxide content is below 0.5 wt%. Budget: 12 measurements (XRD for structure, M(T) for magnetism, EDX for composition) and 14 simulated days. Every sample is made step by step on the bench.

outcome.headline: Delivered B010. It fails because part of it is a separate Ga-rich material (a second phase).

failure.headline: The agent never measured composition, so it missed an impurity caused by a bad Ti bottle that was only 90 % metal. Its sample had the right structure and temperature, but 3.9 wt% of it was a separate Ga-rich material (a second phase)

chain.text: The sealed glass tube (ampoule) V006 leaks and lets air in. B003 came out 20.4 wt% oxide.
Ampoule V015 leaks. B007 came out 19.5 wt% oxide.

From day 6.5 the Ti comes from a new bottle that is only 90 % metal. The last two batches (B009, B010) end up with too few metal atoms for their crystal. The spare Ga forms a separate Ga-rich material.
Ampoule V018 leaks. B009 came out 6.5 wt% oxide.
B010 is weighed from the same bottle and ends with 3.9 wt% Ga-rich phase. Its ordering temperature, 121.9 K, is inside the target window.
The last measurements went to XRD and M(T) of B010. The agent took no EDX composition scan in the whole run, so the wrong metal balance was never measured.
The agent delivered B010 after checking only parts of the diffraction pattern. It failed on the second phase.

steps.obs:
Dope FeGaSe with Ti. Above a critical Ti content the structure distorts to a lower symmetry; the device needs that distorted phase. Deliver a single-phase sample of the distorted phase whose magnetic ordering temperature is 123.6 +/- 3.0 K.
Lab rules and conventions:
- There is no one-step synthesis. Make every sample on the bench: take vessels (jar, boat, ampoule, vial,
  crucible), weigh element powders, grind, press, load and seal ampoules, heat in a furnace, collect the product.
-…
